title: Freeze deterministic zip-barrier facts
conditions: Production implementation may not start until the authoritative IR facts, invariants, ownership, and bounded evidence are frozen.
goal: Select and freeze the smallest existing finite zip-barrier path whose concurrency facts can become explicit and verifiable.
description: Scope: the complete OPT-G design and acceptance artifacts for one independently executable finite zip barrier. Context: lowering and codegen implement selected zip shapes, but frame identity, membership, synchronization, and commit meaning are not yet a single explicit IR contract. Target: freeze one authoritative fact owner, construction and verification invariants, codegen consumption, deterministic EOF behavior, and bounded storage/time evidence. Design Considerations: compare compact immutable metadata with richer graph/event representations and use the simplest structure that preserves verifier-visible facts. Design Value: prevents codegen from guessing concurrency semantics without introducing a scheduler or new runtime queue. Constraints & Risks: preserve active syntax and runtime behavior, complete any metadata migration with no compatibility inference, and leave snapshot joins, queue policies, pressure escalation, and multi-writer merge out of scope.

decisions.composition: one existing finite zip barrier and one authoritative IR fact bundle
decisions.algorithms: direct construction and constant-time invariant checks unless evidence requires more
decisions.data_structures: compact immutable metadata preferred over general graphs or event logs
decisions.state: frame identity, two barrier members, barrier mode, and one commit boundary
decisions.isolation: design and executable acceptance artifacts only
decisions.concurrency: OPT-G follows accepted OPT-F and does not add host scheduling

test_seams: codegen deterministic shortest-input termination and per-frame commit
bounded metadata benchmark or exact counter probe

acceptance_criteria.text: Architecture and Validation freeze one active finite zip scenario, one IR fact owner, construction and verifier invariants, codegen consumption, deterministic EOF behavior, and bounded evidence.
The design compares compact metadata with applicable synchronization graph or event representations and records why the selected structure is sufficient.

commit.message: docs(stream): design OPT-G zip barrier facts

title: Implement explicit finite zip-barrier facts
goal: Preserve and verify explicit deterministic frame and barrier facts for the selected existing finite zip path.
description: Closure: module - deterministic finite zip-barrier IR facts. Context: selected zip shapes execute deterministically but their concurrency meaning is distributed across node fields and codegen control flow. Target: implement the Designer-frozen compact metadata, lowering construction, verifier invariants, codegen consumption, and bounded evidence as the sole fact path. Design Considerations: immutable O(1) metadata, unique lowering ownership, fail-closed verifier checks, shortest-input EOF, and one commit per matched pair. Design Value: makes synchronization semantics inspectable without a scheduler graph. Constraints & Risks: no compatibility inference from legacy fields, no syntax expansion, and no snapshot join, queue, pressure, or merge implementation.

decisions.composition: one compact fact bundle constructed by lowering and consumed by verifier/codegen
decisions.state: no mutable scheduler state; frame facts survive in IR
decisions.isolation: one existing finite zip path only
decisions.concurrency: deterministic barrier semantics independent of host scheduling

acceptance_criteria.text: The selected finite zip path carries one authoritative immutable barrier fact bundle from lowering through verifier and codegen.
Malformed or absent required facts fail closed without compatibility inference, while active finite zip behavior and diagnostics remain stable.
Focused lowering, verifier, codegen, security, and bounded-evidence tests pass.

title: Validate deterministic zip-barrier facts
conditions: Immediate decision issues must be resolved; deferred decisions remain collected for the final OPT-D-G handoff.
goal: Review OPT-G once and run its complete impacted stream-lowering, verifier, codegen, security, benchmark, and documentation regression.
description: Scope: the complete deterministic finite zip-barrier facts group. Context: group completion requires one fresh end-to-end review followed by one impacted regression. Target: prove authoritative facts, verifier enforcement, deterministic shortest-input behavior, per-frame commit, stable diagnostics, and bounded metadata work. Design Considerations: inspect only changed stream-concurrency paths and direct acceptance fixtures. Design Value: closes OPT-G as an explicit IR concurrency boundary. Constraints & Risks: one Reviewer only; no broader IM-D5 feature implementation or repeated full regression without failure evidence.

decisions.composition: one group review then one impacted regression
decisions.isolation: OPT-G changed paths and impacted stream tests

acceptance_criteria.text: No unresolved immediate decision issue remains and the Reviewer confirms the frozen OPT-G boundary.
All impacted lowering, verifier, codegen, security, benchmark, diff, and documentation gates pass once.
